info.name: Student 2 - Applicant Portal and Profiles
info.description:
Postman collection for Student 2 — Applicant Portal and Profiles (LRMIS).

Pre-requisites:
  1. Start MongoDB:  docker start lrmis-mongo
  2. Run Student 1 seed:  python -m app.seed.seed_data
  3. Run Student 2 seed:  python -m app.seed.seed_student2
  4. Start backend:  python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001

Collection variables (edit as needed):
  base_url       — http://127.0.0.1:8001
  applicant_id   — APPL-001  (seeded citizen: Ahmad Khalil)
  application_id — LRMIS-2026-0002  (seeded application with a pending_review document)
  document_id    — DOC-2026-S003  (ownership_deed in pending_review status for LRMIS-2026-0002)

NOTE ON NOTIFICATION STUBS:
  There is no direct HTTP endpoint for reading or creating notification stubs.
  The notification_service.create_notification_stub() function writes to the
  notification_logs MongoDB collection internally. See item 9 for the indirect mechanism.

request.description:
Creates a new applicant profile. Expected result: 201 Created with a generated applicant_id (format APL-YYYY-NNNN) and verification_state 'unverified'.

Applicant types supported: citizen, lawyer, company, surveyor, authorized_representative.
At least one of national_id or registration_number is required in the identity object.
The verification_state defaults to 'unverified' if omitted.

FAILURE EXAMPLE: Duplicate national_id.

This request uses national_id '900512345', which belongs to the seeded applicant APPL-001 (Ahmad Khalil). The applicants collection has a unique sparse index on identity.national_id.

Expected result: 409 Conflict — applicant_service.py checks for a duplicate national_id before inserting and raises an explicit conflict error. FastAPI returns 409 with a detail message indicating the national_id is already registered.

Pre-condition: seed_student2.py must have been run to create the index and APPL-001 record.

query.description: Pass 'applicant' for full self-view (includes privacy_settings, preferences). Pass 'staff' for privacy-filtered view (national_id masked, phone/email hidden if privacy_settings block them).

request.description:
Retrieves the applicant profile for {{applicant_id}} (default: APPL-001).

The viewer_role query parameter controls how much data is returned:
  - viewer_role=applicant  → full self-view: all fields including privacy_settings and preferences
  - viewer_role=staff      → staff view: national_id is masked (e.g. 90*****45), email/phone hidden if applicant's privacy_settings block them

This request uses viewer_role=applicant to demonstrate the full profile response.
Expected result: 200 OK with complete applicant object.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if applicant_id does not exist.

Retrieves the applicant profile in privacy-restricted staff view.

Differences from applicant self-view:
  - national_id is masked: first 2 and last 2 chars shown, rest replaced with *
  - email is null if applicant set privacy_settings.show_email_to_staff = false
  - phone is null if applicant set privacy_settings.show_phone_to_staff = false
  - preferences and privacy_settings fields are omitted from the response

For APPL-001 (Ahmad Khalil), both show_email_to_staff and show_phone_to_staff are true, so both will appear. Compare with APPL-002 (Nour Ibrahim) who has show_email_to_staff=false — their email will be null in staff view.

Returns all land applications linked to the applicant, sorted newest first.

The response includes:
  - applicant_id
  - total count
  - applications array: each item has application_id, application_type, status, parcel_number, zone_id, submitted_at, updated_at, required_next_step

The required_next_step field is the first entry in the workflow.allowed_next array, which tells the applicant what action is expected next.

For APPL-001, the seeded linked_applications is ['LRMIS-2026-0001']. Applications are fetched by querying land_applications where applicant_ref matches the applicant_id.

Expected result: 200 OK with applicant's application list.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if applicant does not exist.

Uploads a supporting document for application {{application_id}} (default: LRMIS-2026-0002).

The application_id is taken from the URL path, not the request body.
The document is created with status 'pending_review' automatically — the uploaded_by field is informational.
A generated document_id (format DOC-YYYY-NNNN) is returned in the response.

The service also:
  - Updates land_applications.submitted_document_types
  - Updates document_status_map for required document types
  - Writes a compatibility stub to the Student 1 'documents' collection
  - Logs to audit_logs and performance_logs

Expected result: 201 Created with full document record.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if the application does not exist in land_applications.

Staff reviews a document and sets its status. Uses {{document_id}} (default: DOC-2026-S003, ownership_deed in pending_review for LRMIS-2026-0002).

Allowed status values: uploaded, pending_review, verified, rejected, missing.
The reviewed_by field is required — it records which staff member performed the review.
The review_note is optional but recommended.

On success, the service also:
  - Updates document_status_map in land_applications to reflect the new status
  - Logs to audit_logs (action: 'document_verified' or 'document_rejected')

Expected result: 200 OK with updated document record including reviewed_at timestamp.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if the document_id does not exist for the given application_id.

To test rejection instead, change status to 'rejected' and update review_note accordingly.

Adds a comment to application {{application_id}} (default: LRMIS-2026-0002).

The actor_type field identifies who is writing the comment: 'applicant' or 'staff'.
The visibility field controls whether the applicant can see the comment:
  - 'applicant_visible' — shown to the applicant (default)
  - 'staff_only'        — internal note, not shown to the applicant

A generated comment_id (format CMT-YYYY-NNNN) is returned.
Comments also appear in the timeline (GET /applications/{id}/timeline) as 'comment_added' events.

Expected result: 201 Created with full comment record including created_at timestamp.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if the application does not exist.

Submits a formal objection against application {{application_id}} (default: LRMIS-2026-0002).

On success:
  - A new objection record is created in the 'objections' collection with status 'submitted'
  - The application status in land_applications is updated to 'under_objection'
  - workflow.current_state is set to 'under_objection'
  - workflow.allowed_next is set to ['legal_review', 'rejected']
  - objection.has_objection is set to true
  - The objection_id is added to objection.objection_ids
  - Events are logged to audit_logs and performance_logs

The reason field is mandatory and must not be empty (min_length=1).

Expected result: 201 Created with objection record (objection_id format: OBJ-YYYY-NNNN).
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if application does not exist.

Returns the full chronological event timeline for application {{application_id}} (default: LRMIS-2026-0002).

The timeline aggregates events from multiple MongoDB collections:
  1. performance_logs.event_stream    — application lifecycle events (submitted, pre_checked, etc.)
  2. land_applications.timestamps     — submitted_at, pre_checked_at, approved_at, rejected_at, completed_at
  3. application_documents            — document_uploaded and document_verified/rejected events
  4. application_comments             — comment_added events
  5. objections                       — objection_submitted events

All events are sorted chronologically by their 'at' timestamp.

Response shape:
{
  "application_id": "LRMIS-2026-0002",
  "current_status": "...",
  "timeline": [
    { "type": "submitted", "at": "...", "actor_type": "applicant", "actor_id": "...", "note": "..." },
    ...
  ]
}

Expected result: 200 OK with timeline array.
Expected failure: 404 Not Found if application does not exist.

NOTIFICATION STUB — INDIRECT MECHANISM:

There is NO direct HTTP endpoint for notification stubs.

This request submits an objection for LRMIS-2026-0001 to demonstrate the 'objection_submitted' trigger event — one of the 5 notification events defined in notification_service.py:
  - status_changed
  - missing_documents_requested
  - document_reviewed
  - objection_submitted
  - certificate_ready

HOW THE STUB WORKS (when fully wired):
The notification_service.create_notification_stub() function in backend/app/services/notification_service.py:
  1. Generates a notification_id (format: NOTIF-YYYY-NNNN)
  2. Writes a record to the notification_logs MongoDB collection
  3. Sets status = 'stub' (no real message is sent)
  4. Stores event_type, applicant_id, application_id, channel, email, phone, message

CURRENT STATUS:
The notification_service function exists and is correctly implemented, but it is NOT yet called from any service or event handler. The wiring between events (objection_service, document_service, workflow_service) and notification_service is not yet implemented.

PRE-SEEDED STUBS:
Run python -m app.seed.seed_student2 to populate notification_logs with 5 example stubs:
  NOTIF-2026-S001 — status_changed       for APPL-001 / LRMIS-2026-0001
  NOTIF-2026-S002 — missing_documents_requested for APPL-002 / LRMIS-2026-0002
  NOTIF-2026-S003 — document_reviewed    for APPL-001 / LRMIS-2026-0001
  NOTIF-2026-S004 — objection_submitted  for APPL-003 / LRMIS-2026-0003
  NOTIF-2026-S005 — certificate_ready    for APPL-004 / LRMIS-2026-0005

Each stub document has: { notification_id, applicant_id, application_id, event_type, channel, email, phone, message: '[STUB] ...', status: 'stub', created_at }

Expected HTTP result: 201 Created (objection is created; the notification stub is an internal side-effect that does not affect the HTTP response).
